cards.prose: The angel says Yahusha (Jesus) will save *his people*, and Ezekiel shows who they are and why he does it. They are the house of Yashar'el (Israel) that went off among the heathen, and Yahuah (the LORD) says he acts *for mine holy name’s sake*. The saving rests on his name and his word, not on anything they had earned.
cards.member_phrase: I do not this for your sakes, O house of Yashar'el (Israel), but for mine holy name’s sake
cards.member_sentence: Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) tells the scattered house that he will act for his holy name's sake, not for theirs.

cards.prose: Moses tells the people plainly that the land does not come to them because of their own goodness. It comes because Yahuah (the LORD) is going to *perform the word which Yahuah (LORD) sware unto thy fathers*. The child named Yahusha (Jesus), Yahuah (the LORD) saves, is that same oath being kept for the sons of those fathers.
cards.member_phrase: Not for thy righteousness, or for the uprightness of thine heart, dost thou go to possess their land
cards.member_sentence: The saving rests on the oath sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, not on the goodness of the people who receive it.

cards.prose: The angel's *his people* is not left vague. Yahusha (Jesus) says who he was sent to when he answers that he is sent only to *the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)*. The one named at his birth for saving his people keeps to that same errand at the end of his teaching.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) himself says he is sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the same people the angel names.

cards.prose: When Yahusha (Jesus) sends the twelve out, he sets the bounds of their errand himself, and the bounds are the same as the angel's *his people*. The one who was named at his birth for saving his people is the one who draws the road for the men he sends.
cards.member_phrase: These twelve Yahusha (Jesus) sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) sends the twelve first to his own people, which is the scope the angel gave at his birth.
cards.flag: The verse's limit on the road (the Gentiles and Samaritans) is left unexplained; I only claimed the errand's scope matches his people.

cards.prose: Ezekiel has Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) say that he himself will *search my sheep, and seek them out*. The angel names the child Yahusha (Jesus), Yahuah (the LORD) saves, and the child is that same shepherd come in the flesh, sent to seek out the people he is saving.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) says he himself will search for his scattered sheep, which is the work Yahusha (Jesus) comes to do.

cards.prose: Who are *his people*? Yahusha (Jesus) answers in his own words, *My sheep hear my voice*. The hearing shows who they were all along. The word goes out wide because the sheep are scattered, and nobody can pick them out by sight.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) says his sheep hear his voice, so the hearing shows who his people are.

cards.prose: The last words of the book send his men to *all nations*, and that does not undo the errand the angel gave at the start. The saving is still for *his people*, and the word goes out among the nations because that is where the scattered sheep now are.
cards.member_phrase: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):
cards.member_sentence: The word is sent out among all nations after the resurrection, to reach the scattered sheep wherever they were driven.

cards.prose: Matthew puts Thamar in the line, and Yahudah's (Judah's) own words explain why she belongs there. He admits *She hath been more righteous than I*, because he had held back his son Shelah from her. The kingly line came through his failure and her claim on him, not around them.
cards.member_phrase: And Yahudah (Judah) acknowledged them, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son.
cards.member_sentence: Yahudah (Judah) admits Tamar was more righteous than he, so the line of the king comes through his own failure and her claim.

cards.prose: Rachab says of Yahuah (the LORD) that *he is Elohim (God) in heaven above, and in earth beneath*. Matthew then names her as the mother of Booz by Salmon, a man of Yahudah (Judah). She came into the line by marrying one of the sons of Yashar'el (Israel), and her confession is where that road began.
cards.member_phrase: for Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), he is Elohim (God) in heaven above, and in earth beneath.
cards.member_sentence: Rachab confesses Yahuah (the LORD) as Elohim (God) in heaven and earth, before she marries Salmon and enters the line.

cards.prose: Ruth ties herself to Naomi and to Naomi's Elohim (God) with *thy people shall be my people*. Matthew names her as the mother of Obed because she then married Booz, a son of Yashar'el (Israel), and the two became one. Her words were the start, and the marriage is what made her one of the people.
cards.member_phrase: thy people shall be my people, and thy Elohim (God) my Elohim (God):
cards.member_sentence: Ruth binds herself to Naomi's people and Naomi's Elohim (God), and her marriage to Booz brings her into the line.

cards.prose: Ruth was a Moabitess, and Moab was born of Lot's daughters. Lot was Abraham's nephew, which puts her people close kin to Abraham's house and not strangers from far away. Even so, what brought her into the line was her marriage to Booz.
cards.member_sentence: Moab came from Lot, Abraham's nephew, so Ruth's people were near kin to Abraham's house.
cards.flag: Moab as near kin to Abraham is said plainly from Lot; Ruth still enters the line only by marriage.

cards.prose: The women bless Yahuah (the LORD) for a kinsman who would see to it that *his name may be famous in Yashar'el (Israel)*. Booz stepped in as the kinsman who buys back what was lost, and in Matthew's list he points ahead to Yahusha (Jesus), the kinsman of the scattered house.
cards.member_phrase: Blessed be Yahuah (LORD), which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.member_sentence: Booz is the kinsman who redeems Naomi's house, and he points ahead to Yahusha (Jesus) as the kinsman of the scattered house.

cards.prose: Matthew could have left her out, or called her by name, and he writes *her that had been the wife of Urias*. That keeps Uriah in view. Samuel's own account says *the thing that David had done displeased Yahuah (LORD)*, so the line to the king is not scrubbed clean.
cards.member_phrase: But the thing that David had done displeased Yahuah (LORD).
cards.member_sentence: Samuel says David's deed displeased Yahuah (the LORD), which is why Matthew names Solomon's mother by her first husband.

cards.prose: Matthew calls him *the son of Abraham*, and here is the promise made to Abraham. Yahuah (the LORD) said that *in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed*. The long list that follows is the road that promise travelled, from Abraham down to Yahusha (Jesus).
cards.member_sentence: The promise to Abraham that all families of the earth be blessed in him is what the genealogy carries down to Yahusha (Jesus).

cards.prose: *The son of David* looks back to what Yahuah (the LORD) promised David, *I will set up thy seed after thee*, and *I will establish his kingdom*. The genealogy then shows that seed arriving as a real line of fathers and sons, all the way down to Yahusha (Jesus).
cards.member_phrase: I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises David a seed and an established kingdom, which Matthew's list traces to Yahusha (Jesus).

cards.prose: Matthew says the line came to Jechonias *about the time they were carried away to Babylon*, and Kings shows what that was. Jerusalem was emptied, and *none remained* but the poorest. The genealogy turns at this wound, and the line goes on in exile.
cards.member_phrase: And he carried away all Jerusalem, and all the princes, and all the mighty men of valour, even ten thousand captives
cards.member_sentence: Kings shows the carrying away to Babylon that Matthew marks, with Jerusalem emptied of its leaders and fighting men.

cards.prose: Long before Babylon, the king of Assyria *carried Yashar'el (Israel) away into Assyria*. Matthew's list passes through Babylon, but the northern house had already been scattered and had not come home. When the list reaches Yahusha (Jesus), the house of Yashar'el (Israel) is still waiting.
cards.member_phrase: took Samaria, and carried Yashar'el (Israel) away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor
cards.member_sentence: The northern house of Yashar'el (Israel) was carried to Assyria well before Babylon and was still scattered when Matthew's list ends.

cards.prose: Matthew counts fourteen generations from the carrying away to Messiah (Christ). Jeremiah had said how long Babylon would hold them, *seventy years*. The captivity was spoken ahead of time by the prophet, so Matthew counts it as part of the road and not as a break in it.
cards.member_sentence: Jeremiah foretold the length of the Babylonian captivity, so the carrying away is part of what was spoken beforehand.

cards.prose: Matthew counts the generations up to Messiah (Christ), and Ezekiel tells what Yahuah (the LORD) does with the two houses. They are written on two sticks and then joined, *And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand.* (Ezekiel 37:17) The Messiah (Christ) the list ends with is the one in whose hand they are made one.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) speaks again to Ezekiel, and what follows is the joining of Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) into one.

cards.prose: The list ends with a people still scattered, and Ezekiel says how that ends. Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) will rule over them *with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm*, and *I will bring you out from the people, and will gather you out of the countries wherein ye are scattered* (Ezekiel 20:34). That gathering is what the Messiah (Christ) is sent for.
cards.member_phrase: As I live, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm
cards.member_sentence: Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) swears he will rule over the scattered house and gather them out of the countries.

cards.prose: Matthew's three sets of fourteen end at Messiah (Christ), and Isaiah says what Yahuah (the LORD) does *the second time*, he sets his hand *to recover the remnant of his people*. The people the angel later says he will save are these scattered ones, called home from Assyria, Egypt, and the islands of the sea.
cards.member_phrase: Yahuah (Lord) shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) sets his hand a second time to recover the remnant of his people from every place they were scattered.

cards.prose: Hosea says both houses are gathered and *appoint themselves one head*. Matthew's list is the account of that head, Messiah (Christ), coming down from Abraham through David. The two houses he is head over are the two houses named here, Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.member_phrase: Then shall the children of Yahudah (Judah) and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) be gathered together
cards.member_sentence: Hosea says Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) will be gathered together under one head, the Messiah (Christ) Matthew names.

cards.prose: Ezra lists the families that *went up out of the captivity*, and Matthew's third set of fourteen runs through that return as well. But it was a partial return to Jerusalem and Yahudah (Judah), and the gathering of both houses that the prophets spoke of was still ahead.
cards.member_phrase: Now these are the children of the province that went up out of the captivity
cards.member_sentence: Ezra lists the families that came back from Babylon, a return to Yahudah (Judah) that fell short of the prophets' ingathering.

cards.prose: Matthew says *Elohim (God) with us*, and John says how it came about. *The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us*. The Word who was with the fathers took a body, and that body is the child to be born of the virgin.
cards.member_phrase: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us
cards.member_sentence: John says the Word became flesh and lived among us, which is how Elohim (God) is with us.

cards.prose: Moses was told *there shall no man see me, and live*. The Father is the one nobody sees. So the one who is born, seen, held, and walked with, the *Elohim (God) with us* of Matthew, is Yahusha (Jesus), the Son who is seen and sent by the Father.
cards.member_sentence: Moses is told no man can see the Father and live, so the one who is seen is the Son.

cards.prose: John states it flat, *No man hath seen Elohim (God) at any time*. The Father is unseen, and the Son *hath declared him*. So when Matthew says *Elohim (God) with us*, it is the Son who is seen and heard, making the Father known.
cards.member_sentence: John says no man has seen the Father and the only begotten Son has declared him.

cards.prose: *Yahuah (LORD) appeared unto him in the plains of Mamre*, and Abraham sat with the one who came. No man has seen the Father, so the one who appeared to Abraham is the Son, the same who is born of the virgin. He walked with the fathers before he was ever carried in Mary's womb.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) appears to Abraham at Mamre, the Son who walked with the fathers long before Mary.

cards.prose: Moses and the elders went up, and *they saw the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Exodus 24:10), and ate and drank. The Father is the one no man sees, so the one they saw was the Son. Matthew's *Elohim (God) with us* is the same one, now born into the flesh.
cards.member_sentence: Moses, Aaron, and the seventy elders go up and see the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), the Son who is seen.

cards.prose: Even at the end, *the Son also himself be subject*, under the one who put all things under him. The Son has a Father and stays under him. So *Elohim (God) with us* is the Father's presence made known in his Son, and not two equals standing side by side.
cards.member_phrase: And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him
cards.member_sentence: At the end the Son is subject to the Father who put all things under him, so the Son has a Father.
cards.flag: The old note's contrast with the co-equal persons frame is left unsaid; I wrote only that the Son is under the Father.

cards.prose: Matthew's *Elohim (God) with us* is the Son, and Paul says who stands over him, *the head of the Messiah (Christ) is Elohim (God)*. The Son is Elohim (God), and he has a Father. That headship did not end when he took flesh.
cards.member_sentence: Paul says the head of the Messiah (Christ) is Elohim (God), so the Son is under the Father even in the flesh.

cards.prose: The name the angel gives is an old one. Moses gave it to Oshea the son of Nun, *Jehoshua*, which carries the Yah of Yahuah's (the LORD's) own name and says that he saves. The child is called by the same name for the same reason.
cards.member_sentence: Moses renames Oshea Jehoshua, an older form of the name Yahusha (Jesus), with the Father's name inside it.

cards.prose: The psalm tells the singers to praise him *by his name JAH*, the short form of the name. That same Yah is the first part of Yahusha (Jesus), so the name the angel gives carries Yah in it and says what he has come to do.
cards.member_sentence: The psalm calls the singers to praise him by his name Yah, which is the first part of the name Yahusha (Jesus).

cards.prose: After Moses died, Yahuah (the LORD) spoke to *Joshua the son of Nun* to lead the people into the land. He bears the same name as the child Joseph is told to call Yahusha (Jesus). The first one led the people in, and this one comes to bring the scattered home for good.
cards.member_sentence: Joshua, who bears the same name as Yahusha (Jesus), is commissioned to lead the people into the land.

cards.prose: The angel gives the name, and Paul says where it ends up, *a name which is above every name*. The name Yahusha (Jesus) was given at the birth to say that Yahuah (the LORD) saves, and Elohim (God) raised the one who carries it to the highest place.
cards.member_sentence: Paul says Elohim (God) exalted him and gave him a name above every name, the name given at his birth.

cards.prose: Matthew writes *Jesse begat David the king*, and here is how that came about. Yahuah (the LORD) sends Samuel to Jesse because *I have provided me a king among his sons*. The king did not rise by his own reaching. He was provided, and the line to Yahusha (Jesus) runs through him.
cards.member_phrase: fill thine horn with oil, and go, I will send thee to Jesse the Beth-lehemite: for I have provided me a king among his sons.
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) sends Samuel to anoint a king from among Jesse's sons, the founding of the king's line.

cards.prose: Matthew says Solomon came from the wife of Urias, and this is where it began. The army was out at war, and *But David tarried still at Jerusalem*. Matthew's list does not hide how Solomon came to be.
cards.member_phrase: But David tarried still at Jerusalem.
cards.member_sentence: The account of David and Bath-sheba begins with the king staying home while the army fights, which is the root of Matthew's phrase.

cards.prose: Josias is the last king Matthew names before the carrying away, and Kings shows what followed him. Pharaoh Nechoh put Eliakim on the throne and *turned his name to Jehoiakim*, and carried Jehoahaz off to Egypt. Kings were being set and removed by foreign hands before Babylon ever came.
cards.member_phrase: And Pharaoh-nechoh made Eliakim the son of Josiah king in the room of Josiah his father, and turned his name to Jehoiakim
cards.member_sentence: After Josias, Pharaoh sets and removes the kings of Yahudah (Judah), the falling apart that leads to Babylon.

cards.prose: Matthew's *Jechonias* is the Coniah of Jeremiah, and Yahuah (the LORD) says that even if he *were the signet upon my right hand*, he would pluck him off. Matthew still lets the line run through him, and then tells that the child was conceived of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit).
cards.member_phrase: As I live, saith Yahuah (LORD), though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Yahudah (Judah) were the signet upon my right hand
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) pronounces judgment on Coniah, the Jechonias of Matthew's list, though the line still runs through him.
cards.flag: The old note reads the Jechonias curse as bypassed by Joseph's legal adoption; I kept to the texts and said only that the child was conceived of the Ruach HaKodesh, a working reading to settle.

cards.prose: Matthew tells the conception from Joseph's side and Luke tells it from Mary's, beginning where *the angel Gabriel was sent from Elohim (God)* to Nazareth. It is one event told from two doorways, and the two accounts agree on whose child this is.
cards.member_sentence: Luke begins the same conception from Mary's side, with Gabriel sent to Nazareth.

cards.prose: Joseph knew what the Torah says where *a damsel that is a virgin be betrothed* and is found with another man. Being a just man he was not willing to make her a public example, and the Torah itself gave him the quiet road he chose.
cards.member_sentence: The Torah speaks of a betrothed virgin found with another man, the exposure Joseph's quiet course would have spared Mary.

cards.prose: The Torah lets a man give *a bill of divorcement* into her hand. Matthew says Joseph was *minded to put her away privily*, which means a written paper and no public trial. He stayed inside the Torah and spared her.
cards.member_phrase: then let him write her a bill of divorcement, and give it in her hand, and send her out of his house.
cards.member_sentence: The bill of divorcement is the Torah's quiet way for Joseph to put Mary away without exposing her.

cards.prose: Elohim (God) spoke to Jacob in a dream, with angels going up and down, and now the angel of Yahuah (the LORD) speaks to Joseph *in a dream*. It is the same way he guides his own. Jacob's dream carried the promise to his seed, and Joseph's carries it to the child.
cards.member_sentence: Jacob's dream at Beth-el shows an angel of Elohim (God) giving direction in a dream, as Joseph is given.

cards.prose: The first Joseph was a dreamer, and *Joseph dreamed a dream* that steered the course of his father's whole house. This Joseph is given word in a dream too, and before the story is far along he also goes down into Egypt with the seed of promise in his keeping.
cards.member_sentence: The patriarch Joseph received word in dreams, as Matthew's Joseph does.

cards.prose: *Then was the secret revealed unto Daniel in a night vision*. Yahuah (the LORD) has often opened hidden things to his servants by night, and Joseph's dream is of that kind. The hidden thing, how the child was conceived, is opened to him by an angel.
cards.member_sentence: Daniel is shown a hidden thing in a night vision, the same way Joseph is shown the secret of the conception.

cards.prose: The angel calls him *thou son of David*, and those words point to what Yahuah (the LORD) promised David, *I will set up thy seed after thee*. Joseph is the man through whom David's house is handed to the child, as he takes Mary and names him.
cards.member_phrase: I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.
cards.member_sentence: The angel's name for Joseph, son of David, points to the promise of a seed and a kingdom.

cards.prose: Joseph did as he was told and took his wife, and Luke tells what followed, that she bore *her firstborn son* and wrapped him in swaddling clothes. Matthew goes on to say Joseph named him Yahusha (Jesus). The birth Luke describes is the birth Joseph's obedience made room for.
cards.member_sentence: Luke gives the birth of the firstborn son that Joseph's obedience in taking Mary made room for.

cards.prose: A firstborn belongs to Yahuah (the LORD), *it is mine*. Joseph takes his wife and the child is her firstborn, so the child comes under that word of the Torah. Yahusha (Jesus) was set apart as a firstborn son of Yashar'el (Israel), in the Torah's own way.
cards.member_sentence: The Torah sets every firstborn apart to Yahuah (the LORD), which is the standing of the child Mary bears.

cards.prose: Paul calls the firstborn *the image of the invisible Elohim (God)*. The Father is the one no man sees, and the firstborn Mary bore is his image, the one who can be seen. The word Matthew uses for the child reaches this far.
cards.member_sentence: Paul calls the firstborn the image of the invisible Father, so the child Mary bore is the Father's image.
cards.flag: Cards 3248 and 3249 carried one shared old note; the two Colossians verses are split here, one for the image of the Father and one for the firstborn from the dead.

cards.prose: Paul calls him *the beginning, the firstborn from the dead*. The same word that names the child born to Mary names the one who rose first from the grave. The firstborn of Joseph's household is the first to rise.
cards.member_sentence: Paul calls the firstborn the head of the body and the firstborn from the dead, the one with the highest place.

new_threads.title: The carrying away to Babylon, and the house still scattered
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. The turn in Matthew's list was spoken of and written down long before he set it in his book.

*And Josias begat Jechonias and his brethren, about the time they were carried away to Babylon:* (Matthew 1:11)

Babylon was not the first captivity. The northern house of Yashar'el (Israel) had been taken out of the land well before, and it never came home in a body.

*In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Yashar'el (Israel) away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.* (2 Kings 17:6)

Then Yahudah (Judah) was taken in her turn, and the land was emptied of nearly everyone who could lead it.

*And he carried away all Jerusalem, and all the princes, and all the mighty men of valour, even ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and smiths: none remained, save the poorest sort of the people of the land.* (2 Kings 24:14)

Jeremiah had already said how long it would last, so the captivity was not an accident that broke the line.

*And this whole land shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.* (Jeremiah 25:11)

Some did go home, but it was a partial return to Jerusalem and Yahudah (Judah), and nothing like the gathering of both houses that the prophets describe.

*Now these are the children of the province that went up out of the captivity, of those which had been carried away, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away unto Babylon, and came again unto Jerusalem and Yahudah (Judah), every one unto his city;* (Ezra 2:1)

That is why Matthew counts the way he does.

*So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations; and from the carrying away into Babylon unto Messiah (Christ) are fourteen generations.* (Matthew 1:17)

The count runs straight through the carrying away and ends at Messiah (Christ). The line of the king is shown walking through exile, with the northern house still scattered and the return still ahead.
